projects.title: This Portfolio: Full-stack Site with Its Own CMS
projects.description: The site you're on: a Next.js portfolio backed by a database, with a mobile-first admin panel, role-based login, uploads, analytics and an AI assistant that answers questions about my experience.
projects.objective: Replace a static, hard-coded portfolio with one I can update from my phone in a minute, without redeploying, while keeping it fast, secure and cheap to run (free hosting tiers).
projects.approach: Server Components render every page straight from the database, so edits appear on the next page load. A REST API validates every write with Zod schemas shared by the API and the admin UI. Login uses salted scrypt password hashes and signed, HttpOnly session tokens checked by a single proxy in front of /admin and /api, with admin and editor roles and a protected owner account. Uploads (resume, photos) are checked by file content, not just extension, and phone photos are resized in the browser before upload. Database changes are additive migrations that run automatically on every deploy.
projects.architecture:
Browser (site + admin panel)
        │
   Next.js on Vercel
   ├─ proxy.ts  → auth gate for /admin and /api
   ├─ Server Components → pages
   └─ Route handlers → REST API
        │  Prisma + libSQL
        ▼
   Turso (hosted SQLite)
        │
   Claude API ← "Ask my resume"
projects.result: Content, images and resume are editable from a phone. Every push to main deploys automatically and migrates the database. It runs on free tiers with no surprise-bill risk, and it includes visit and contact analytics plus an AI assistant grounded only in the site's own content.

projects.title: Hybrid Code Search for a Talk-to-Code Assistant: RAG, BM25 and Re-ranking
projects.description: Why a code assistant needs more than vector search, and how combining semantic search, BM25 keyword search and re-ranking improves the answers.
projects.content:
## The goal
A VS Code prototype that answers questions about a codebase, right inside the editor. [Add: which codebase, who it was for.]

## Why vector search alone falls short for code
Semantic search finds code that means the same thing, but exact names (function names, config keys, error codes) often need keyword matching.

## The approach
- Index code chunks in a vector database for semantic search
- Run BM25 keyword search alongside it
- Merge the candidates and re-rank them before sending the best ones to the model (RAG)
